title: Tic-tac-toe with an unbeatable minimax AI
prompt:
Build a command-line tic-tac-toe game in Python where a human (X) plays against the computer (O).

Modules:
- board.py: `class Board`. Cells are numbered 0-8, left to right, top to bottom.
  - `make_move(index, player)` places `"X"` or `"O"`. X always moves first and players must alternate. Raises `ValueError` if the index is outside 0-8, the cell is occupied, it is not that player's turn, or the game is already over.
  - `current_player()` returns `"X"` or `"O"`, whoever moves next.
  - `winner()` returns `"X"`, `"O"` or `None`.
  - `is_full()` returns True when all 9 cells are taken.
  - `available_moves()` returns a sorted list of empty cell indexes.
  - `copy()` returns an independent copy of the board.
- ai.py: `best_move(board) -> int` returns an optimal move for the player whose turn it is, using minimax. It must take an immediate win when one is available, otherwise block the opponent's immediate win, and it must never lose.
- main.py: game loop. Read X's moves (cell numbers) from standard input, one per line. After each valid X move the computer plays O using best_move. Print the board after every move. An invalid move prints a line starting with `Error:` and reads the next line. When the game ends print exactly one final line: `Winner: X`, `Winner: O` or `Draw`. Exit cleanly at end of input.

Constraints: use only the Python standard library. The entry point is main.py in the project root, guarded by `if __name__ == "__main__":`.
